parakeet: When people mistake emotional power for epistemic validity, they substitute filling for thinking, reward simplicity over inquiry, and elevate personal comfort over shared truth. This isn't just a personal error, it has cultural consequences. Religions, conspiracy theories, political ideologies, and superstitions all thrive in environments where incredulity goes unchallenged and arrogance is mistaken for insight. We are often more persuaded by what feels true than by what actually is true. And that's why the ethical call to think, truly think, matters more now than ever.
